name: READACCT.jcl
description:
The JCL job READACCT reads account data from a VSAM KSDS file and extracts/transforms the records into three different sequential output files: a compressed fixed-block file, an array-based fixed-block file, and a variable-block file. The job first cleans up any pre-existing output files before executing the main account data extraction program CBACT01C.Key Functionalities:
Deletes any pre-existing versions of three output datasets (PSCOMP, ARRYPS, VBPS) before processing to ensure clean output files
Reads account data from the VSAM KSDS source file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ACCTDATA.VSAM.KSDS) containing customer account records
Writes account records to a compressed sequential fixed-block output file (PSCOMP) with a record length of 107 bytes
Writes account records to an array-format sequential fixed-block output file (ARRYPS) with a record length of 110 bytes
Writes account records to a variable-block sequential output file (VBPS) with a maximum record length of 84 bytes
All three output files are newly created, cataloged, and allocated with 1 primary cylinder and 2 secondary cylinders of disk space

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The READACCT account data processing job is initiated for a new run and the PREDEL step is the first step to execute
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The PREDEL step runs at the start of the job before any account data extraction begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All three account data output files must be deleted — the Compressed Account Data File (PSCOMP), the Array-Structured Account Data File (ARRYPS), and the Variable-Block Account Data File (VBPS) — so that no stale or residual account data from any prior job run is carried forward into the current run

rules.Rule_Name: PREDEL - IEFBR14 - Pre-Processing Cleanup of Account Data Output Files
rules.Rule_Description: Before each new account data processing run begins, all three account data output files from any previous run must be removed to guarantee a clean and uncontaminated processing environment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The PREDEL step is executing and is processing the three account data output files — Compressed Account Data File (PSCOMP), Array-Structured Account Data File (ARRYPS), and Variable-Block Account Data File (VBPS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The PREDEL step completes either normally (successful termination) OR abnormally (failed termination)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All three account data output files must be deleted in both the success path and the failure path — no account data output file should be retained regardless of how the cleanup step ends

rules.Rule_Name: PREDEL - IEFBR14 - Unconditional Deletion of Account Data Output Files on Any Step Outcome
rules.Rule_Description: The deletion of all three account data output files must occur unconditionally — whether the cleanup step itself ends successfully or encounters a failure — ensuring no residual account data files survive under any circumstance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The PREDEL step is attempting to delete the three account data output files — Compressed Account Data File (PSCOMP), Array-Structured Account Data File (ARRYPS), and Variable-Block Account Data File (VBPS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Any one or all of the three account data output files do not exist in the system at the time of the cleanup step
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cleanup step must not produce an error or cause the job to fail — non-existent files must be treated as already deleted, and the job must continue normally to the account data extraction step (STEP05)

rules.Rule_Name: PREDEL - IEFBR14 - Graceful Handling When Account Data Output Files Do Not Exist
rules.Rule_Description: If any or all of the three account data output files do not exist at the time of the cleanup step (e.g., first-time job run or files were already removed), the cleanup step must not fail or raise an error, and must allow the subsequent account data extraction step to proceed normally.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Master Account Database (VSAM Key-Sequenced Account Dataset — ACCTFILE) is available and accessible in shared mode allowing concurrent access by other processes, AND the three target output files — Compressed Account Data File (OUTFILE), Array-Structured Account Data File (ARRYFILE), and Variable-Block Account Data File (VBRCFILE) — have been pre-deleted and are ready to be freshly created in this run
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Data Extraction program (CBACT01C) is executed to read all account records from the Master Account Database and write them into three simultaneously produced output files
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: 1. All account records are read from the Master Account Database (ACCTFILE) in shared mode without exclusively locking it from other concurrent processes. 2. A new Compressed Fixed-Length Account Data File (OUTFILE) containing 107-byte fixed-length records is created as a brand-new sequential file and permanently cataloged in the system upon successful completion. 3. A new Array-Structured Fixed-Length Account Data File (ARRYFILE) containing 110-byte fixed-length records is created as a brand-new sequential file and permanently cataloged in the system upon successful completion. 4. A new Variable-Block Account Data File (VBRCFILE) containing variable-length records of up to 84 bytes is created as a brand-new sequential file and permanently cataloged in the system upon successful completion. 5. If the extraction process fails for any reason, ALL three output files (OUTFILE, ARRYFILE, VBRCFILE) are automatically and immediately deleted — no partial, incomplete, or potentially corrupt account data files are retained or made available to downstream consumers. 6. All processing messages and operational logs are written to the system output console (SYSOUT and SYSPRINT) for audit trail and monitoring purposes.

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05 - CBACT01C - Account Data Extraction and Multi-Format Output Generation
rules.Rule_Description: This step invokes the Account Data Extraction program (CBACT01C) to read all account records from the Master Account Database and simultaneously produce three differently structured sequential output files — a compressed fixed-length file, an array-structured fixed-length file, and a variable-length file — to serve different downstream consumers. All three output files are retained only upon successful completion; any failure results in automatic deletion of all outputs to prevent partial data propagation.
